title: mcp: validate_expression answers ok for label() on a field without options, which the authoring door refuses, because both bridges strip field options (#28659 follow-up)

Filing gate: ① a class (b) out-of-scope finding from the #28659 dev (os-dev-report 6559671824, PR #28714). Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the grade.

Reach: an AI agent or MCP client that checks a formula with the MCP `validate_expression` tool before saving it.
Reader who acts: `domain:server` (the MCP expression tool and its bridges).

## What happens

After PR #28714, the authoring door refuses `label(record.FIELD)` on a field that declares no options (422 `expression-invalid`, naming the field). The MCP `validate_expression` tool judges the same expression, but the object schema it receives has no field options, because both bridges strip them. So the tool still answers ok for an expression the door then refuses. An agent that trusts the tool learns of the refusal only when it saves.

## Wanted

`validate_expression` gives the same answer the door gives for the same object and expression: the bridges pass field options through to the one judge, and no second check is added. Test: `label(record.first)` on a text field reads as refused, naming `first`, through MCP and at the door alike; `label()` on a select reads ok on both.

Dedupe: searched `validate_expression options`, `mcp validate_expression label`; no open card.
